content: Rifampin induces the activity of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which can significantly alter the metabolism of various drugs. Below are the detailed effects of rifampin on specific drugs and the recommended clinical actions: 1. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Rifampin reduces the plasma levels and therapeutic effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by increasing their metabolism via CYP3A4. This reduction may increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 2. BCG Vaccine (Live): Rifampin decreases the efficacy of the BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 3. Bedaquiline: Rifampin lowers the levels and efficacy of bedaquiline by enhancing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers should not be used with bedaquiline due to the risk of reduced therapeutic effects. 4. Bosutinib: Rifampin decreases bosutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 85% through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Brigatinib: Rifampin reduces the levels and efficacy of brigatinib by increasing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 6. Budesonide: Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Buspirone: Rifampin reduces the levels and therapeutic effects of buspirone by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 8. Cabozantinib: Rifampin decreases cabozantinib levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase the cabozantinib dose (40 mg/day for Cometriq or 20 mg/day for Cabometyx) and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the inducer. 9. Capivasertib: Rifampin reduces capivasertib exposure and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Capmatinib: Rifampin decreases capmatinib levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 11. Carbamazepine: Rifampin reduces carbamazepine levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Ceftobiprole Medocaril Sodium: Ceftobiprole increases rifampin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 13. Ceritinib: Rifampin decreases ceritinib levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Cilostazol: Rifampin reduces cilostazol levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 15. Cinacalcet: Rifampin decreases cinacalcet levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Clopidogrel: Rifampin increases the metabolism of clopidogrel to its active metabolite via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor for increased antiplatelet effects when coadministered. 17. Clozapine: Rifampin reduces clozapine levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 18. Colchicine: Rifampin decreases colchicine levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Conivaptan: Rifampin reduces conivaptan levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 20. Conjugated Estrogens: Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Dabigatran: Rifampin reduces dabigatran levels and efficacy by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration. 22. Dabrafenib: Rifampin decreases dabrafenib levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Daridorexant: Rifampin reduces daridorexant levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 24. Darolutamide: Rifampin decreases darolutamide levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 and P-gp metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 25. Darunavir: Rifampin reduces darunavir levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 26. Dasatinib: Rifampin decreases dasatinib levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Deflazacort: Rifampin reduces deflazacort levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. 28. Deuruxolitinib: Rifampin decreases deuruxolitinib levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Dexamethasone: Rifampin reduces dexamethasone levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 30. Diazepam: Rifampin decreases diazepam levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Diltiazem: Rifampin reduces diltiazem levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or adjust dosage with close monitoring if necessary. 32. Dronedarone: Rifampin decreases dronedarone levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Duloxetine: Rifampin reduces duloxetine levels and effects by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 34. Duvelisib: Rifampin decreases duvelisib levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Edoxaban: Rifampin reduces edoxaban levels and effects by inducing P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration. 36. Elacestrant: Rifampin decreases elacestrant levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Erythromycin: Rifampin reduces erythromycin levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 38. Estradiol: Rifampin decreases estradiol levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Ethinylestradiol: Rifampin reduces the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives containing ethinylestradiol. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 40. Etrasimod: Rifampin decreases etrasimod levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Everolimus: Rifampin reduces everolimus levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-gp efflux transporters. Coadministration is contraindicated. 42. Felodipine: Rifampin decreases felodipine levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Fexinidazole: Rifampin increases fexinidazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 44. Fineranone: Rifampin reduces fineranone levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Fludrocortisone: Rifampin decreases fludrocortisone levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 46. Fosamprenavir: Rifampin reduces fosamprenavir levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 47. Fosaprepitant: Rifampin decreases fosaprepitant levels and efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This list highlights the significant interactions between rifampin and various drugs, emphasizing the need for careful consideration of alternative therapies or dosage adjustments to maintain therapeutic efficacy and minimize adverse effects.
